skill.name: next-cache-components-adoption
skill.description: Turn on Cache Components in a Next.js app and resolve the blocking routes it surfaces. Use when the user wants to enable, adopt, or migrate to Cache Components, flip the `cacheComponents` flag, work through a flood of blocking-prerender / instant validation errors, run the `cache-components-instant-false` codemod, or decide between opting routes out with `export const instant = false` and fixing them in place.
skill.summary: Guide a Next.js App Router project through staged Cache Components adoption and route verification.
skill.author: vercel

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, framework identifiers, documentation links, and benign local commands. The skill still directs agents to run mutable packages and install a canary skill without approval, creating supply-chain and unauthorized-change risk. It also recommends sharing route screenshots without privacy or redaction checks.

remediation.issue: The skill directs agents to install next-dev-loop without user approval.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit consent before installation, pin an immutable commit, and present the source and planned changes before execution.

remediation.issue: Codemod commands execute mutable latest and canary package versions.
remediation.suggestion: Pin reviewed package versions and require approval before network execution or bulk repository modifications.

remediation.issue: Browser screenshots may contain sensitive application or user data.
remediation.suggestion: Request consent, inspect each image, redact sensitive values, and share only the minimum required view.

content.value_statement: Cache Components migrations can expose blocking routes and hidden rendering issues. This skill guides staged adoption, route fixes, browser checks, and final build verification.
actual_capabilities: Checks Next.js version and App Router prerequisites before migration.
Guides enabling Cache Components and translating incompatible route settings.
Supports staged codemod adoption or direct route-by-route migration.
Identifies request-time reads, synchronous I/O, and invalid cache boundaries.
Verifies routes through development overlays, browser behavior, and production builds.
Documents deliberate blocking exceptions and remaining migration work.
limitations: Requires a runnable App Router application using Next.js 16.3 or later.
Does not migrate Pages Router routes to the App Router.
Build-only verification cannot confirm streamed content or the visible static shell.
External documentation and codemods require network access and explicit dependency approval.

use_cases.title: Prepare an application migration
use_cases.description: Assess prerequisites, incompatible settings, and startup blockers before enabling Cache Components.

use_cases.title: Plan reviewable migration stages
use_cases.description: Separate the baseline opt-out change from feature-level adoption and verification work.

use_cases.title: Validate rendering behavior
use_cases.description: Check static shells, streamed content, sibling routes, and final production builds.

prompt_templates.title: Assess migration readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this Next.js app for Cache Components readiness. Report the version, router type, incompatible settings, startup blockers, and recommended approach. Do not edit files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a read-only readiness review.

prompt_templates.title: Create a passing baseline
prompt_templates.prompt: Enable Cache Components with a staged migration. Ask before installing tools. Preserve behavior, run only approved codemods, and stop after a passing baseline build.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a small initial change before route adoption.

prompt_templates.title: Adopt one feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Adopt Cache Components for [feature]. Remove opt-outs top-down, fix documented blockers, verify each route in development and the browser, then run a focused build.
prompt_templates.scenario: Migrate one product area end to end.

prompt_templates.title: Complete and audit adoption
prompt_templates.prompt: Complete the migration across the app. Preserve security gates, document intentional blocking routes, test sibling routes, and provide a route verification table.
prompt_templates.scenario: Finish a complex application migration with traceable evidence.

output_examples.input: Assess whether this application is ready for Cache Components.
output: The application uses the App Router and meets the required Next.js version.
Two route settings need translation before the feature can be enabled.
The application must start successfully with its local database before verification.

output_examples.input: Migrate the account settings feature using staged adoption.
output: The shared layout and profile page now pass development validation.
Request-specific content streams inside focused suspense boundaries.
The feature build passes, and one intentional blocking route is documented.

output_examples.output: Every migrated route passes the production build. Browser checks confirm useful static shells, resolved streamed content, and no remaining undocumented opt-outs.

best_practices: Ask before installing skills, packages, or repository-writing tools.
Migrate layouts before pages and verify sibling routes after shared changes.
Use both browser checks and production builds before marking a route complete.
anti_patterns: Do not remove incompatible settings without preserving their intended behavior.
Do not move authentication or authorization gates behind suspense boundaries without approval.
Do not treat a passing build as proof that streamed pages render correctly.

faq.question: Which projects can use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it with runnable App Router projects on Next.js 16.3 or later. Pages Router migration is outside its scope.

faq.question: Does the skill edit application files?
faq.answer: Yes. It can change configuration, route exports, cache boundaries, and suspense placement after the user approves the approach.

faq.question: Should I choose staged or direct adoption?
faq.answer: Choose staged adoption for smaller reviewable changes. Choose direct adoption when one branch and a larger combined change are acceptable.

faq.question: Is browser access required?
faq.answer: Browser access is strongly recommended for streamed routes. Build-only checks cannot confirm the visible static shell or resolved content.

faq.question: How are security gates handled?
faq.answer: The skill should preserve authentication and authorization behavior. It asks the user before changing gates whose purpose is unclear.

faq.question: What marks the migration complete?
faq.answer: The build passes, browser checks succeed, migration markers are resolved, and every remaining blocking route has a documented reason.
